prompt:
Hey, I need you to write the campaign retrospective for the MC Evolution Sprint. You're the Retrospector agent. This is critically important.

Context: we just ran our first ever coordinated 4-agent campaign on Mission Control. 4 agents (Orchestrator, Beacon, Compass, Overwatch) worked simultaneously. A lot went right, a lot went wrong, and we learned a ton. I need you to distill this into broadly applicable lessons.

Your task: produce a retrospective that answers:
1. What patterns made this campaign succeed? (What should we ALWAYS do in future campaigns?)
2. What patterns caused failures? (What should we NEVER do again?)
3. What was the single biggest insight from this entire sprint?
4. How should the orchestrator role work differently next time?
5. What should the campaign Setup phase look like to prevent missed items?
6. Rate this campaign: was it worth running 4 agents simultaneously?

Read these files to understand what happened:
- C:\Users\ephra\phredomade\.claude\agent-hub\campaigns.json (wins, losses, remaining)
- C:\Users\ephra\phredomade\.claude\agent-hub\findings.json (all findings, especially f023-f032)
- C:\Users\ephra\phredomade\.claude\agent-hub\coordinated-sprint\agent-b-output.md (Compass analysis)
- C:\Users\ephra\phredomade\.claude\agent-hub\coordinated-sprint\agent-c-output.md (Overwatch analysis)
- C:\Users\ephra\phredomade\CLAUDE.md (behavioral rules)

Your retrospective must be BROADLY APPLICABLE. Not "we should have wired the /why page" but "orchestrators must audit all agent output files for accessibility after a sprint." Think principles, not incidents.

Write your output to: .claude/agent-hub/coordinated-sprint/retrospective.md

DON'T modify any existing MC code or data files. You're analyzing and writing.

Start by reading everything, then produce the retrospective.
